description:
Owner 2026-10-19: the full snapshot run produced the load it then refused (load 2.40 before, 4.26 after; all 57 reports not quiet). The runner is sequential, so no example overlaps another; the load comes from (a) the 1-min load average lagging a minute or more after the example's own cc compile and the previous report, (b) the measured process's own threads counted in the after-load, (c) macOS load counting more than CPU use (idle laptop: load 1.74, all processes 0.47 cores).

Plan:
1. Quiet test on other processes' CPU, not the load average: sum ps %cpu over every process outside the bench's own tree (the example process, its children, the mix runner). Limit DEFK_BENCH_QUIET_CPU, default 1.0 core (to be checked by a probe).
2. Settle before each measured report (Defk.Bench, cache miss): poll every 2 s until other-CPU is quiet for several samples in a row, max wait (about 120 s), then measure; print the wait. A report that never settles is measured and marked not quiet, as now.
3. Quiet after: other-CPU after the measurement, same test.
4. The snapshot row's quiet = all its reports were quiet; the run line records other-CPU, not the whole-run load average.
5. Probe first: one --bench --only run, log both signals per report, then pick the limit.

Blocks defk-9p7 (the first stored scoreboard waits for this).
title: Bench quiet test: settle before each report, count only other processes' CPU
